For a long time, climate, weather, and Earth system research have relied almost entirely on numerical simulations. Supercomputers are tasked with solving physical equations layer by layer, where the precision, resolution, and stability of the models determine how much of the natural system humans can "see clearly." In recent years, with changes in computing power, artificial intelligence has increasingly been introduced into these traditional fields. Particularly in climate and Earth system modeling, AI is held with high expectations: can it fill in the details that numerical models struggle to cover? Can it provide a finer view of the system under limited computing power? These questions are becoming unavoidable discussions in the fields of supercomputing and scientific computing.

Earth system models are among the most representative scenarios in this regard. From global circulation to local weather, from oceans to the atmosphere, and from kilometer-scale to more subtle changes, the processes these models need to handle are extremely complex and nearly impossible to fully exhaust. Precisely because of this, the academic and engineering communities have maintained a cautious, even divided, attitude toward how AI should be integrated into Earth system modeling.

At the GAIR 2025 conference, discussions surrounding the relationship between artificial intelligence and scientific computing were once again brought to the forefront. Professor Fu Haohuan shared insights during the event, exploring the boundaries and possibilities between numerical simulation and AI in the context of Earth system models and supercomputing practices. excerpt_i18n.en: Cloud providers are now at a critical juncture to break through. After years of fierce competition, the cloud market has become suffocatingly constrained—relentless price wars, projects resistant to standardization, and high-investment business models that are difficult to scale have trapped providers in a quagmire. Could large models, repeatedly hyped by the market, be the key to escaping this predicament? Many believe so, but the path forward remains unclear. On December 18–19, ByteDance’s Volcano Engine held its 2025 Winter Force conference, showcasing new advancements like the Doubao large model 1.8 and the video generation model Seedance 1.5 pro, aiming to carve a "channel" through the industry’s rigid barriers and channel the "living water" of AI into the sector. It can be said that Agent represents today’s "super consensus" for AI breakthroughs, yet how to develop Agents remains a "diverse narrative" with varied opinions among providers. The Agent Infra platform—"AgentKit"—is Volcano’s answer to this major challenge. While there are many Agent developer platforms today, what is the logic behind Volcano’s development of AgentKit? Clues may have long been hidden in the history of Volcano Engine’s evolution. Volcano’s MaaS reaching the top spot is largely due to seizing the AI dividend. In 2025, which cloud provider leads in MaaS? The answer is undoubtedly Volcano Engine.

On December 23, the globally authoritative AI benchmark platform Artificial Analysis released its latest image model rankings. Alibaba's 6B-parameter Z-Image Turbo surpassed the 32B FLUX.2 to become the top open-source image generation model. Currently, the model is available on Alibaba Cloud's Bailian platform, costing only $5 to generate 1,000 images.

Z-Image Turbo overtook FLUX.2 to top the Artificial Analysis image model rankings. According to official data from Artificial Analysis, Z-Image Turbo achieved an ELO score of 1152, setting a new record on the leaderboard. Industry experts consider it one of the best-performing, fastest-generating, and most affordable image generation models available.

Z-Image Turbo supports deployment on consumer-grade graphics cards with 16GB of VRAM. In an H100 deployment environment, it can generate images comparable to those produced by models with tens of billions of parameters in just one second. In terms of output quality, the model significantly enhances the realism of images, finely restoring details such as skin texture, hair strands, and fabric materials. It also improves bilingual text rendering capabilities in Chinese and English, maintaining clear text and natural layouts even in challenging scenarios like small fonts, complex typography, or poster designs.

Z-Image Turbo is capable of generating hyper-realistic images and bilingual Chinese-English posters.
